site.title: Arcade Patches
site.tagline: Translation and restoration patches for arcade fighting games.
intro: Fan-made patches for arcade games, mostly Japan-only CPS-2 and NAOMI releases. Everything is distributed as a patch against your own dump of the original game — binary diffs (IPS), MiSTer MRA overlays, or data-free GD-ROM patches; no game data is hosted here.
Everything on this site was built and verified against real MAME sets, with automated acceptance runs and human review of every change.
site.contact_note: For questions, corrections, or takedown requests, open an issue on the GitHub repository.
site.author: Steve Gordon

patches.title: Night Warriors 2
patches.subtitle: Vampire Hunter 2 — English translation
patches.summary: A complete English translation of the Japan-only Vampire Hunter 2, presented as the Night Warriors 2 that never shipped outside Japan.
description: Vampire Hunter 2 is a 1997 Capcom fighter that only ever reached Japanese arcades. Its predecessor came to the West as Night Warriors: Darkstalkers' Revenge, but this sequel never made the trip. This patch translates the whole game into English and gives it the Western name it should have had: Night Warriors 2.

The Night Warriors 2 title screen isn't a fan mock-up. An unused Western title was already tucked away inside the original game — the patch finishes it and switches it on, leaving the gameplay exactly as it was.

Where Capcom's own English wording exists in the Western Darkstalkers games, the patch reuses it so the writing matches the official localization. Everything else — the victory taunts, the boss exchanges, and every character's ending — is freshly translated and checked in the actual game.
changes: Arcade-native Night Warriors 2 title screen, built from the ROM's unused Western title path
USA region presentation (warning screen and region byte)
Western character names on character select, route map labels, and the fight HUD: Zabel → L.Raptor, Gallon → J.Talbain, Lei-Lei → Hsien-Ko, Phobos → Huitzil, Aulbath → Rikuo
All boss dialog and every character ending translated (44 records, verified on natural routes)
English staff roll under the Night Warriors 2 name

screenshots.caption: Title screen. The arcade-native Night Warriors 2 logo, completed from the unused Western title path in the original ROM.
Character select. Phobos becomes Huitzil, his official Western name.
Post-fight quotes — all 225 messages are in English (Anakaris shown).
Ending narration in English, captured on a natural playthrough route (Pyron's ending shown).

notes: MAME reports checksum warnings for the three patched program ROMs. This is expected; the game boots and plays normally.
Official English donor text comes from the Western Night Warriors and Vampire Savior arcade sets and is only used where the Japanese source record was demonstrably equivalent.

patches.title: Vampire Savior 2
patches.subtitle: English translation
patches.game: Vampire Savior 2: The Lord of Vampire (Japan 970913)
patches.summary: English translation of the Japan-only Vampire Savior 2: Western character names, all 241 post-fight quotes, and every ending and final-boss dialog page.
description: Vampire Savior 2 is a Japan-only update of Vampire Savior with a shuffled roster — Donovan, Huitzil, and Pyron join the fight, while Gallon, Aulbath, and Sasquatch sit this one out — plus its own set of endings. It never came out in English. This patch translates the entire game.

Where the dialogue matches the Western release of Vampire Savior, the patch reuses Capcom's own English so it reads like the official localization. The lines unique to this version — the quotes for Huitzil, Pyron, and Donovan, along with every ending and the final confrontation with Jedah — are newly translated to read naturally while staying true to the original.
The title screen keeps the Vampire Savior 2 name, which is how the game appeared in arcades. 'Darkstalkers 3' was a later name used only for the home versions.
changes: Western character names on character select, route map, and fight HUD: Bulleta → Baby Bonnie Hood, Zabel → L.Raptor, Lei-Lei → Hsien-Ko, Phobos → Huitzil
All 241 post-fight quotes in English (192 official arcade records reused verbatim, 48 VS2-only records newly translated)
All 29 ending pages and both 4-page Jedah final-boss dialogs translated and relocated into verified free ROM space
Route stage names and option labels verified byte-identical to the official U.S. arcade records

screenshots.caption: Bulleta under her Western name, Baby Bonnie Hood.
Post-fight quotes in English (B.B. Hood shown, natural route capture).
The same ending page before and after: the Japanese source and its relocated English translation.
The title art is intentionally unchanged — the official U.S. arcade release of the previous game also used Vampire Savior branding.

notes: Release candidate: the translation is complete and every changed surface has passed automated acceptance, but wording review is still open. Report anything that reads badly.
MAME reports checksum warnings for the three patched program ROMs. This is expected; the game boots and plays normally.

patches.title: Street Fighter Alpha 3 Upper
patches.subtitle: NAOMI GD-ROM multi-region patch
patches.summary: Removes the Japan-only region lock from the Zero 3 Upper GD-ROM so it boots on Japanese, USA, and Export NAOMI systems. One byte in the game header, properly re-encrypted.
description: Street Fighter Zero 3 Upper is an enhanced version of Street Fighter Alpha 3 that only came to arcades in Japan, on Sega's NAOMI hardware. Because it's flagged as a Japanese release, a US or Export machine rejects the disc on sight with "THIS GAME IS NOT ACCEPTABLE BY MAIN BOARD."

This patch flips that region flag so the very same disc boots on Japanese, US, and Export systems. Nothing about the game itself changes — but on a US or Export machine it now shows its Western Street Fighter Alpha 3 branding instead of the Japanese Street Fighter Zero 3, exactly as an overseas release would have.

It's the smallest change possible: only the region flag is touched, and the game, its language, and its settings are left just as Capcom shipped them. Booting was confirmed on all three region setups.
changes: NAOMI header region mask: Japan → Japan + USA + Export (one byte in the game header, eight encrypted bytes on disc)
Nothing else — this is a region unlock only; it does not translate or otherwise modify the game

screenshots.caption: The same patched disc on two BIOS regions. The game's own region-dependent title art shows Street Fighter Zero 3 on a Japanese board and Street Fighter Alpha 3 on a USA board — note the U.S. copyright line under the American title.
A USA-region NAOMI BIOS: the original Japanese GD-ROM is refused; the patched image is accepted and loads.

notes: Applying the patch requires chdman (bundled with every MAME release) and about 2.5 GB of temporary disk space.
MAME reports a checksum warning for the patched CHD. This is expected; the game boots and plays normally.
For optical drive emulators on real hardware, the patched CHD can be unpacked to GDI with chdman extractcd.
You still need the unchanged sfz3ugd.zip (security PIC) alongside the CHD.

patches.title: Street Fighter Alpha 3 Upper
patches.subtitle: NAOMI GD-ROM rebuild
patches.game: Street Fighter Zero 3 Upper (Japan, NAOMI GD-ROM, sfz3ugd)
patches.summary: Conversion tooling that turns a GD-ROM image from your own copy of the Japan-only Zero 3 Upper arcade game into multi-region Alpha 3 Upper builds.
description: Street Fighter Zero 3 Upper shipped on NAOMI GD-ROM only in Japan. This project builds tooling that takes a GD-ROM image from your own copy of the arcade game and rebuilds it into a working multi-region image, including the converted character portraits the Western versions need.
In development. The container format work (Capcom ARC v7, IBIS payloads) and GD-ROM DES tooling are done; build and verification automation is in progress.
notes: This will ship as a conversion tool, not a binary patch: it works from a GD-ROM image of the arcade game you own.

patches.title: Street Fighter Alpha 2 Gold
patches.subtitle: Zero 2 Dash — native CPS-2 reconstruction
patches.game: Street Fighter Alpha 2 Gold / Street Fighter Zero 2 Dash (PS2 anthology revision, 2006)
patches.summary: Recovering the revised 2006 PlayStation 2 edition of Alpha 2 Gold as a native CPS-2 game, by differential restoration from the released Zero 2 Alpha arcade program.
description: The 2006 PlayStation 2 anthology contains a revised edition of Street Fighter Alpha 2 Gold / Zero 2 Dash that never existed on arcade hardware. The goal here is a native CPS-2 68K game — not a PS2 emulator wrapper and not a newly designed remix — recovered by starting from the released CPS-2 Zero 2 Alpha program and restoring the bounded anthology changes one at a time.

Research stage. Boot, title, character-select presentation, and the restored Cammy path are being validated with deterministic MAME automation; there is no release yet, and there may never be one if the restoration cannot be proven faithful.
